_description: Single source of truth for the add-on's version. Everything user-facing that shows a version reads from here (see `surfaces`), and `test/ui/version-manifest.test.js` fails if any of them drift. Update this file in the same commit as the release, never separately.
_line: Releases are 2.0.X builds (docs/versioning.md §1): each release takes the next X. The line moves to 2.1 only when the owner explicitly asks for it; `VERSION_LINE` in test/ui/version-manifest.test.js changes in the same commit.
_previous: 1.0.0 is Sefaria for Google Docs 1.0, the Marketplace add-on this one follows. Development builds before 2.0.0 carried 2.1.0 and earlier numbers; they were never published, and those numbers are retired.
_prefsSchemaVersion: Must equal PREFS_SCHEMA_CURRENT_ in apps-script/migrations.gs. This is the user-data schema, not the add-on version: it only ever increases, and it increases whenever a new preference key ships. It was not reset with the version numbers and must never be. A mismatch means either a migration landed without a version bump or the reverse — both leave upgrading users in a state no migration covers.
_surfaces: Every place the version string is shown to a user. An agent bumping the version must update all of them; the manifest test checks they agree.

surfaces.note: About tab meta-pill. Shows MAJOR.MINOR only — 2.0.X builds do not change it.
Shown on install and from the release-notes dialog. MAJOR.MINOR only; a 2.0.X build adds its notes under the same heading.

_changelog: docs/CHANGELOG.md carries a `## v<version>` heading for this version. While 'pending-release' the heading ends '(release pending)' and `released` is null; at release, set status 'released', the ISO date in `released`, and the same date in place of '(release pending)'. Work after that collects under `## Unreleased` until the next 2.0.X build consolidates it.
_deployment: Apps Script has no manifest version field — appsscript.json carries no version. `clasp push` replaces the script project's HEAD, which only test deployments run. Users run the numbered script version (from `clasp version`) that the Marketplace SDK App Configuration points to, so a release is: live-test HEAD, `clasp version`, set that number in the SDK. Neither Apps Script version numbers nor the SDK record which add-on version a number corresponds to — this file, together with the `clasp version` description (use `v<version>`), is the only record, which is exactly why it must not drift.
